h1: The 6 Best RAB Motion Sensor Lights of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best RAB Motion Sensor Lights: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 RAB motion sensor flood lights compared on detection pattern, color temperature, adjustability and voltage for homes and sites.
summary: The RAB GT500RW/L is the best residential choice: 3600 lumens from two 38W lamps with a switchable 3000K, 4000K or 5000K color temperature. The LU160 Luminator is the value pick, with adjustable sensitivity, range and hold time. The STL360HW/L covers approaches from every angle, and the GT500 hardwired suits 277V sites.
intro: A motion light that triggers when a car passes the road or a cat crosses the lawn trains its owner to ignore it, and then it protects nothing. The sensor pattern, and your ability to tune it, matter far more than raw lumens. Most buyers compare brightness, then discover that the light fires at the wrong things.

RAB's flood light line fits that problem well, because the range spans fixed patterns from 110 to 360 degrees and adjustable units that let you trim range and hold time. We ranked six RAB models by how well each pattern matches a real entrance, how much control you have, and what the light looks like at night. All six are hardwired fixtures, so installation is part of the decision.

products.name: RAB Lighting GT500RW/L LED Motion Sensor Flood Light
products.verdict: 3600 lumens from two 38W PAR38 lamps with selectable 3000K, 4000K or 5000K light at 90 CRI.
products.description:
The GT500RW/L is the one RAB where the light itself is as adjustable as the sensor. Two 38W PAR38 lamps produce 3600 lumens, and you choose 3000K, 4000K or 5000K, which covers warm porch light up to cool security white. A 90 CRI rating means colors, such as a car or a package, look natural, and it mounts to a wall.

It wins because color control is rare on motion floodlights and it makes the fixture suit a house. Against the STL360HW/L, which has the same 3600 lumens and 90 CRI, it gives up the 360 degree sensor but costs less, at $100 to $200. The LU160 beats it on sensor tuning but offers a fixed color.

Best for porches and walls where a neutral tone beats cold white. One gap: the detection angle is missing from its specs.
products.idealFor: Residential porches and walls where a warm or neutral tone beats cold white.
products.skipIf: You need fine control over sensor range.

products.name: RAB Lighting LU160 Luminator Motion Sensor Flood Light
products.verdict: Adjustable sensitivity, range and hold time, dual aimable heads and an IP65 wet rating at $50 to $100.
products.description:
The LU160 treats the sensor as the main feature. You can adjust sensitivity, range and hold time, which are the three controls that stop false triggers. Dual aimable heads let you point light at a gate and a path separately, the housing carries an IP65 wet location rating with sealed gaskets, and a dusk to dawn photocell prevents daytime firing.

It ranks second because the listing gives no lumen or color figure, so you cannot compare brightness against the 3600 lumen RAB models. Its edge is the price, in the $50 to $100 bucket, and the fact that it solves the most common complaint. Against the GT500RW/L, it trades color control for sensor control.

Best for yards near streets, walkways or pets. The caveat is that you must set it up carefully, because default settings may still false trigger.
products.idealFor: Yards near streets, walkways or pets where false triggers are the main complaint.
products.skipIf: You want to choose the color of the light.

products.name: RAB Lighting STL360HW/L Motion Sensor Flood Light
products.verdict: 180 degrees outward and 360 degrees straight down. Watches corners and entries from every approach.
products.description:
The STL360HW/L combines 180 degree outward detection with 360 degree coverage straight down, so it sees a person walking toward the building and one standing directly beneath the fixture. Dual 38W LED PAR38 lamps give 3600 lumens at 90 CRI, a dusk to dawn photocell handles daylight, and an LED indicator shows when the sensor is detecting.

It ranks third because its price, in the $200 to $500 bucket, is the highest in the ranking and it offers no color selection. Against the STL200H/L, it covers directly below the fixture as well as wide, so it suits corners. Against the GT500RW/L, you pay more for sensing pattern rather than light quality.

Best for building corners and entries approached from several sides. The caveat is that wider coverage means more triggers from passing cars or wildlife.
products.idealFor: Corners and entries where people can approach from the sides or from directly beneath.
products.skipIf: A single door faces one direction.

products.name: RAB Lighting STL200H/L Motion Sensor Flood Light
products.verdict: 200 degree side-to-side detection with dual 38W LED lamps and 3600 lumens at 90 CRI.
products.description:
The STL200H/L spreads detection across 200 degrees side to side, which is wide enough for a garage front or a wall of a building. It uses the same dual 38W LED PAR38 lamps, 3600 lumens and 90 CRI as the STL360HW/L, and adds an on-guard detection indicator and a photocell.

It ranks fourth because a wide arc is only useful on long faces. Without the straight-down coverage of the STL360HW/L, someone close to the wall can slip under the sensor. It also costs the same $200 to $500 as that model, so you need the arc to justify it. Against the STL110HW/L, it covers nearly twice the width.

Best for long garage fronts and building faces. The caveat is that wide arcs on fences near neighbors may wake them, so trim the aim.
products.idealFor: Long garage fronts and building faces approached from a wide arc.
products.skipIf: People tend to approach directly under the fixture.

products.name: RAB Lighting STL110HW/L Motion Sensor Flood Light
products.verdict: A 110 degree forward pattern with a Double Look Down lens, 3600 lumens and a photocell.
products.description:
The STL110HW/L watches 110 degrees forward and adds a Double Look Down lens to catch someone near the base of the wall. It pairs dual 38W LED PAR38 lamps with 3600 lumens at 90 CRI, a dusk to dawn photocell and an LED indicator, priced in the $100 to $200 range.

Fifth place reflects that a narrow pattern fits fewer locations than the wider RABs. At a front door where visitors walk straight up the path, though, 110 degrees is exactly right, and the lower price than the 360 and 200 degree models makes sense. It matches their light output but gives up coverage and any adjustment.

Best for front and side doors with one approach direction. No tuning controls appear in its specs, so range and sensitivity are whatever RAB sets at the factory.
products.idealFor: Front and side doors where visitors approach from one direction.
products.skipIf: Your entrance is a corner with several approaches.

products.name: RAB Lighting GT500 Hardwired Motion Sensor Flood Light
products.verdict: 110 degree coverage for 120V or 277V supply, with 6000V surge protection.
products.description:
The GT500 is the commercial-style RAB: 110 degree coverage, operation on 120V or 277V, load ratings of 600W at 120V and 1350W at 277V, and 6000V surge protection. The listing gives load ratings instead of lumens, so lamp choice is a separate decision.

It ranks last because it is the least complete package for a typical house. There are no lumen, color or lamp details to compare against the 3600 lumen models, and the strengths are electrical: 277V capability and surge protection. For a shop, outbuilding or commercial site on 277V, those are the whole point, and the $50 to $100 price is attractive.

Best for outbuildings and commercial-style sites. The caveat is that you must confirm your supply voltage and select compatible lamps, so it is not a plug-in upgrade for most homes.
products.idealFor: Outbuildings, shops and commercial-style sites with 277V power.
products.skipIf: You want a complete lit fixture for a house.

whatMatters.detail: A sensor sees an arc, not a circle. A 110 degree pattern suits a single door, 200 degrees covers a garage front, and 360 degrees below with 180 outward covers a corner. Match the arc to where people actually walk, and check whether the listing mentions look-down coverage. Sensors mounted high often miss someone standing right below, which is exactly where a prowler would be.

Sensitivity sets how large a heat source triggers the light, range sets how far it looks, and hold time sets how long it stays on. The LU160 adjusts all three. Fixtures that list none of these use factory defaults, which can mean false triggers from cars and animals. Look for named dials or settings in the specs, since a vague line about adjustability usually describes only the head angle.

Lumens measure brightness, and 3600 is plenty for a door or yard. Color temperature changes the feel: 3000K is warm, 5000K is cool white. The GT500RW/L offers all three. Look for CRI too, as 90 renders colors accurately, which helps a camera or a neighbor describe a car's paint correctly. Confirm the lamps are included and whether the fixture lets you change the color temperature later.

Residential supply is 120V, while commercial sites often use 277V. The GT500 handles both. Confirm your supply, check the load rating against your lamps, and be ready to hardwire. If you are unsure, an electrician should make the connection. Read the listing for a wiring diagram or box type, and switch off the breaker, not just the wall switch, before touching the fixture.

An IP65 rating, as on the LU160, means dust-tight and protected against water jets. Fixtures marked wet location in their model name, such as the HW series, are intended for outdoor mounting. Look for a stated rating in the listing before mounting under open sky. Sealed gaskets and a downward-facing head keep rain out of the lamp socket, which is where cheap fixtures fail first.

faq.q: Can I install a RAB motion light myself?
faq.a: These are hardwired fixtures, so you connect them to your supply. If you are comfortable with household wiring, it is straightforward, but the GT500 and its 277V option should be installed by an electrician.

faq.q: Why does my motion light keep turning on for no reason?
faq.a: Heat sources like cars, animals and sun on walls trigger it. The LU160 lets you lower sensitivity and range. On the fixed-pattern models, re-aim the heads and shrink the coverage with a different mounting spot.

faq.q: Is the STL360HW/L worth it over the STL110HW/L?
faq.a: Only at corners. The STL360HW/L adds 360 degree downward and 180 degree outward coverage, while the STL110HW/L watches 110 degrees forward. For a single front door, the cheaper model does the job.

faq.q: How do I get a warmer light from the GT500RW/L?
faq.a: Choose the 3000K setting. It also offers 4000K and 5000K options. Warm light suits porches and brick walls, while 5000K gives a cooler security look.
Yes, unless you want the light firing in daylight. The STL360HW/L, STL200H/L, STL110HW/L and LU160 list dusk to dawn photocells. Confirm it on any model you pick.

faq.q: Can the GT500 run on household power?
faq.a: Yes. It supports 120V and 277V, with load ratings of 600W at 120V and 1350W at 277V. The 277V rating matters mainly for commercial sites and outbuildings.

finalTake: For most houses the RAB Lighting GT500RW/L is the best motion floodlight here: 3600 lumens with a choice of 3000K, 4000K or 5000K. The LU160 Luminator is the right buy if false triggers are your problem, the STL360HW/L covers awkward corners, and the GT500 hardwired belongs on 277V sites.
